passage: Ten p.m. before the science practical, and Wasim was still shaking with anger. Vaibhav had copied his lab report again, and the teacher had praised the neat diagram as Vaibhav's. Without thinking, Wasim typed into the class group: “Funny how some people's own work looks exactly like other people's homework.” He hit send and dropped the phone on the bed. By 10:20 there were twelve replies, all guessing. By 10:30 Vaibhav's name was in the chat, and someone had called him a cheat. By morning the rumour said Wasim had proof and had already reported him. Vaibhav met him at the gate: “You could have just told me.” The teacher, who had wanted a quiet word about the report, now had a shouting match in the corridor to deal with, and the practical started late.

qa.q: What did Wasim type into the class group?
qa.a: Wasim typed: Funny how some people's own work looks exactly like other people's homework.

qa.q: What was Wasim feeling when he sent the message?
qa.a: Wasim was angry and, in the heat of it, wanted to hit back without thinking.

qa.q: What could Wasim do instead of posting?
qa.a: Wasim could speak to Vaibhav privately and, if it continued, tell the teacher, since copying is a matter for the teacher and not for the class group.

qa.q: How might Vaibhav feel on seeing his name in the group?
qa.a: Vaibhav would feel humiliated and angry, and his words You could have just told me show he was hurt at being shamed in public.

grounding: An angry teen posts a hint about the cheater in the class group, which humiliates the friend, spreads rumours and turns a matter for the teacher into a fight.

Uday was furious by the time he got home to their flat in Kolkata. Irawati, his friend since Class Five, had copied the whole science answer from the girl in front and scored one mark more than him. He had studied till one in the morning.
Before dinner he typed in the class group: “Some people in 9B should thank their neighbours for their marks. You know who you are.” He hit send.
In ten minutes there were forty replies. Guesses, names, laughing faces. Someone wrote Irawati's name. Someone else named a different girl, who had nothing to do with it. By morning a rumour was going round that Irawati's parents had paid for her marks.
At school Irawati wouldn't look at anyone. The girl wrongly named was in tears. The class teacher called Uday in, not to talk about copying but about the post. What should have been a quiet word with the teacher was now a fight the whole class was part of.

qa.q: What did Uday type in the class group?
qa.a: Some people in 9B should thank their neighbours for their marks. You know who you are.

qa.q: What was Uday feeling when he hit send?
qa.a: Uday was furious and resentful, having studied till one only to be beaten by a copied answer.

qa.q: What could Uday have done instead of posting?
qa.a: Talk to Irawati privately or tell the class teacher calmly, keeping it a quiet matter instead of a public fight.

qa.q: How was the next day for the girl who was wrongly named?
qa.a: She was in tears, hurt by a rumour about something she had nothing to do with.

grounding: Shows an angry teen hinting about a cheating friend in the class group, which humiliates her, spreads rumours and turns a matter for the teacher into a fight.

“Why did you post that, Binita?”
“Because you copied, Sharmila! Everyone should know.”
“Everyone does know now. Thirty people guessed. Half of them guessed Anu, who didn't do anything. Anu's mother called the school.”
“I didn't name anyone.”
“You didn't have to. ‘Some toppers should thank their neighbours'? Everyone knew. My brother saw it. He asked me at dinner if I'm a cheat.”
“...Are you?”
Sharmila looked at the floor. “I copied once. In that test. I was going to tell Ma'am myself, today.”
“Oh.”
“Now Ma'am wants to see both of us. Not about the copying. About the group. You made it a fight.”
Binita's face went hot. “I was just angry.”
“I know. You could have just told me you were angry."

qa.q: Who did half the class guess?
What was Binita feeling when her face went hot?
qa.a: Binita felt embarrassed and a bit ashamed, seeing that the angry post had hurt more people than intended.

qa.q: What else could Binita have done while angry?
qa.a: Tell Sharmila directly, or go to Ma'am privately, instead of hinting in a group of thirty.

qa.q: How was the post for Sharmila?
qa.a: Sharmila was humiliated, questioned at home by her brother, and lost the chance to own up to Ma'am first.

grounding: Shows an angry teen hinting about a cheating friend in the class group, which humiliates her, spreads rumours and turns the matter into a fight.
